## Comparison Table

| | **Canva Pro** ⭐ | **Adobe Creative Cloud** | **Affinity (by Canva)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Price** | $180/yr = **$15/mo** exactly at budget; $18/mo if billed monthly. Free tier is genuinely usable | Express Premium **$9.99/mo**; single apps (Photoshop/Illustrator/InDesign) **$22.99/mo**; CC Pro **$69.99/mo** ($34.99 first 3 mo) | **Free for individuals** ("Zero bucks given") |
| **Fits $15/mo budget?** | ✅ Yes (annual) | ⚠️ Only Express Premium; full apps are 1.5–4.5× over | ✅ Yes ($0) |
| **Ease of use (no design background)** | ✅ Best — drag-and-drop editor, no learning curve | ⚠️ Express is easy; Photoshop/Illustrator/InDesign are steep | ❌ Hardest — pro-grade Vector/Pixel/Layout tool aimed at trained designers |
| **Templates (social + print)** | ✅ 1.6M+ free / **3.6M+ with Pro**, 1,000+ design types, incl. menus & flyers | ✅ Large library in Express; the pro apps are template-light | ❌ Not template-driven — you build from scratch |
| **Logo creation** | ✅ Templates + Brand Kit (5 kits on Pro) | ✅ Illustrator is best-in-class but hard to learn | ✅ True vector tools, but manual |
| **Print-ready menus** | ✅ Print-ready PDF export + built-in print ordering (10% off on Business) | ✅ InDesign is the print standard, at $22.99/mo | ✅ Strong layout/CMYK control |
| **Platform** | Browser + apps (works anywhere) | Desktop + web | Mac, Windows, iPad only — no Linux |

## Recommendation: **Canva Pro at $180/year ($15/mo)**

**Why it suits Grace specifically:**

1. **It lands exactly on budget** — $15/mo when paid annually, and she can start any day. Adobe's real design apps (Illustrator for a logo, InDesign for menus) would cost $45+/mo combined.
2. **No design background required.** This is the deciding factor. Affinity is free, but it's a professional tool with three technical modes — the same tool a trained designer would use instead of Adobe. Grace would spend weeks learning it instead of baking.
3. **Templates do the design work.** 3.6M+ templates covering Instagram posts, menus, and logos means she starts from a professionally designed layout and just swaps in her bakery's name, photos, and colors.
4. **One tool covers all three jobs** — social graphics, logo, and print-ready menu PDFs — with the Brand Kit keeping fonts and colors consistent across everything.

**A money-saving tip worth flagging:** Grace should **start on Canva Free** (or use Pro's free trial) for a few weeks. The free tier includes 1.6M+ templates and a basic Brand Kit, which may be enough. She only needs Pro for premium templates, background removal, resizing one design across formats, and social scheduling.

**Two caveats on the research:** Adobe Express Premium at $9.99/mo is a legitimate cheaper alternative with a similar template-based approach — worth a look if she wants to save $5/mo, though its template library is smaller. And since Canva now owns Affinity, **Canva Free already includes access to Affinity** — so choosing Canva doesn't rule Affinity out later if she grows into it.
